payload.friendly_name: Landed worktree cleanup and upgrade worktree scope
payload.purpose_context: Landing worktrees and their local branches pile up after their PRs merge because no step removes them; one clone held 48 stale worktrees using about 36 GB. Upgrade then writes and commits into every one of them, including open PR branches. This Mission gives operators a provable, offline prune surface and makes upgrade leave non-Mission worktrees alone unless named (#7173).
payload.purpose_tldr: Report and safely prune worktrees whose work has landed, and stop upgrade committing into non-Mission worktrees by default.

payload.question: Where should removal of landed worktrees live?

payload.final_answer: A provable prune command plus runbook and skill steps; post-consolidate report deferred.

payload.question: New doctor worktrees, or extend doctor workspaces?

payload.final_answer: Extend doctor workspaces with a --prune option, documented properly; --fix keeps its husk contract.

payload.question: What should upgrade do with non-Mission worktrees by default?

payload.final_answer: Skip by default; opt in per worktree with a new flag; preview and output name every worktree and its disposition.

payload.question: Is an offline proof of landed enough?

payload.final_answer: Offline only: lane_tip.is_absorbed against the local origin/<primary> ref, no fetch, no GitHub lookup; fail closed without git >= 2.38.

payload.question: Should --prune also delete the landed worktree's local branch?
How is 'no process inside the worktree' proven?
What is the upgrade opt-in flag?

payload.final_answer: Yes, after the same proof (git branch -D only after absorption proof; recreate command printed)
/proc scan; where unprovable the worktree is report-only

payload.question: How does --prune remove a worktree given the destructive guard's chokepoint uses --force after its own clean proof?
How does --prune delete a landed branch whose commits exist on no other ref (rebase merge with the remote head auto-deleted)?

payload.final_answer: Guard gains a no-force mode: same clean proof, then plain git worktree remove
New LANDED named intent passed only by the prune after the absorption proof; tip recorded under refs/spec-kitty/discarded/<branch> when commits are unique; routing pin gains one caller

payload.wp_title: Destructive guard: no-force removal and LANDED branch intent
